note: Asked after the final test and before the score is shown (so the score can't colour the answers); not after the delayed test. Scales run 1 to 7. 'lightScale' is the manipulation check (2026-11-13, a scale in place of the choice 'lights', where 2 of 4 pilot learners chose "I'm not sure"): in the direct condition the practice's right/wrong light is about the learner's own answers (expected near 1), in the recursive one about Kai's (near 7). 'calls' (recursive only, `condition`): what the learner's call on Kai's answer rested on, to tell trusting Kai from not reading its steps (the pilot's calls matched the light 6 of 12 times). 'leak': whether Kai seemed to know something it wasn't told (the leak check's view from the learner). 'help': notes or other help besides a dictionary, against the rule that everything is from memory. Three open questions follow (2026-11-05, for the qualitative analysis, in the course's recommended form: a specific moment, what was done next, one decision and its reasoning); optional, not timed. 'beforeCall' (2026-11-17, recursive only, open): how the learner went about a problem before calling Kai's answer, before the light (an answer of their own first, a skim of Kai's steps, or a close reading), in their own words beside the choice 'calls'. Last (2026-11-16, moved from the results page so the questions after the test are one list, not one round after another): anything else the learner wants to tell us, also logged as the feedback event. The rating of the session (1 to 5) was asked before it until 2026-11-17, when it went as a near duplicate of 'enjoy'. The results page keeps its own feedback box only when no questions were asked (the follow-up test, or the survey switched off).

items.prompt: How much effort did you put into teaching Kai?
How responsible did you feel for how well Kai learned?
How well do you think you now understand how greedy and UCB choose?
How much did the practice problems help you learn?
How much did you enjoy the session?
In the practice problems, the right/wrong light told me mostly about…
When you called Kai's answer right or wrong, what did you mostly go on?
options: I checked Kai's steps against what I knew
I worked out the answer myself and compared
Kai sounded sure, so I went with it
A guess: no time or energy to check

items.prompt: Did Kai ever seem to know something you hadn't told it?
Besides a dictionary, did you use anything during the session?
What, if anything, helped you understand how greedy and UCB choose?
Where, if anywhere, did you run into difficulty?
In the practice problems, what did you do before you called Kai's answer right or wrong?
items.hint: For example, whether you worked out your own answer first, skimmed Kai's steps or went through them carefully. Any way is fine: tell us what you actually did.

items.prompt: In the practice problems, how did you decide what to do after an answer was marked wrong?
items.hint: Describe one moment and your reasoning.

items.prompt: Anything else you would like to tell us?
items.hint: What was confusing, what Kai did well or badly, anything the questions above didn't cover.
